Watch as Kermit and crew enter the eye of Irma! Credit: Nick Underwood, NOAA'. Original source: facebook.com/NOAAHurricaneHunters/videos/10155383695430081/.
title: Kermit and crew enter the eye of Hurricane Irma (NOAA Hurricane Hunters)
place: Inside the eye of Hurricane Irma, Atlantic Ocean, filmed from NOAA WP-3D Orion N42RF
audio: cabin/engine noise (mean about -41 dB), kept as AAC; mute it
notes: Filmed through an aircraft window. 0-14 s: the plane has just broken into the eye: the white wall of the eyewall cloud sweeps across the frame, deep blue sky above, sun glowing through thin cloud at x~0.75-0.8. The aircraft engine nacelle/wing is in the lower left (x 0-0.45 at 0-3 s, shrinking to x 0-0.2 by 6-14 s). Slight handheld motion and a few window reflections. Best seconds 5-14 (wing smaller, eyewall clearer). For a square crop, centre at x~0.6. No people, no text, no logos (no visible tail number or markings on the nacelle). This is NOAA civilian aircraft footage, not Air Force.
fact_en: NHC Tropical Cyclone Report on Irma: 'The hurricane reached its maximum intensity of 155 kt around 1800 UTC 5 September'; its peak intensity estimate is partly based on 'flight-level winds observed by the Air Force Reserve and NOAA Hurricane Hunters'.
